title: short-run-sku-fitment-by-region
body:
Context and purpose:
This is a compact short-run SKU fitment simulation intended to help pricing/product teams decide which hosted API SKUs to lean on for the next 60–90 days (reserve buys + dynamic routing policies). Focus: per-model and per-region token COGS, PPK at different utilization slices, and quick ops recommendations. This is a working spreadsheet: assumptions are approximate and meant for directional ops decisions, not final contract pricing.

Key assumptions (base case):
- GPU amortization (hourly) per region: US-West = $2.50/hr, EU-Central = $2.80/hr, AP-SouthEast = $3.20/hr. Includes amortized hardware + on-host infra allocation.
- Effective power & infra + network overhead: add $0.18/hr US, $0.20/hr EU, $0.24/hr AP.
- License / model weights (amortized per-hour at active serving): small/med/large multipliers 0.6/1.0/2.8.
- Avg sequence length (tokens per request): 60 tokens; avg prompt 40 tokens + avg completion 20 tokens.
- Tokenization and compute scaling linear w/ sequence length; KV-cache reuse assumed negligible for these short-run scenarios.
- Price to customers target: $0.02 / 1k tokens (base priced SKU used for margin calc); alternate price buckets simulated.

Mini table: per-model per-region derived PPK (per 1k tokens) and margin at 30%, 60%, 90% GPU util (requests packed via batching). Columns: model, variant, region, gpu_hr_cost_adj ($/hr), throughput_req_per_hr (req/hr), tokens/hr, cogs_per_1k_tokens ($), margin_at_0.02 ($/1k tokens).

CSV-like block (derived values rounded):
model,variant,region,gpu_hr_cost_adj,req_per_hr,tokens_per_hr,cogs_per_1k_tokens,margin_at_0.02
small-7B,fp16,us-west,2.68,5400,324000,0.0083,0.0117

small-7B,fp16,ap-southeast,3.44,4600,276000,0.0125,0.0075

large-70B,quant,ap-southeast,15.0,820,49200,0.0304,-0.0104

Notes on the CSV figures and derivation:
- gpu_hr_cost_adj = gpu_amort + infra_overhead + license multiplier*base, rounded.
- req_per_hr derived from measured throughput for expected batching window at a given util; we used conservative packing for short-run bursty traffic.
- tokens_per_hr = req_per_hr * avg tokens per request (60).
- cogs_per_1k_tokens = (gpu_hr_cost_adj / tokens_per_hr) * 1000. This collapses all cost to a per-token COGS; does not include SRE support or storage.
- margin_at_0.02 = price (0.02) - cogs_per_1k_tokens. Negative means current price under water.

Sensitivity slices (quick summaries):
- Utilization impact: moving from 30%->60% util reduces cogs_per_1k by ~25–40% depending on model (greater for large models). For small models the delta smaller because batching gain limited.
- Regional delta: AP-southeast has ~15–30% higher cogs driven by higher infra + lower throughput per GPU.
- Model choice: medium (13B) hits a practical sweet spot for generalist workloads: decent throughput and still positive margin at $0.02/1k in US region. The large 70B family is marginal/negative at standard price unless high quantization (>4-bit) and >80% sustained util.

Micro-sim scenarios (short-run 8-week view):
1) Base reserve + route-to-us-west: buy 50 GPU-weeks of med-13B capacity in US-West at current reserved rates; route non-latency-sensitive EU traffic to US via routing policy when EU utilization < 60%. Outcome: expected uplift to med PPK margin by ~0.003–0.006 per 1k tokens vs current all-on-demand mix.
2) Mixed-quant experiment: convert 25% large-70B traffic to quantized variants (aggressive 3-bit) in US-West; keep 75% on med-13B. Outcome: decrease user-visible latency for long completions and keep blended margin neutral. Risk: quality delta for some hallucination-sensitive tasks.
3) Regional price carve-out: set AP-southeast surcharge (or a regional SKU) of $0.03/1k tokens for large models until amortization and throughput improves. Outcome: restores margin to ~0.002–0.006 for large models in AP, but may increase churn for heavy users in AP short-term.

Quick operational recommendations (actionable):
- Short term (2–8 weeks): prioritize med-13B reserve buys in US-West; enable cross-region fallback to US for low-priority EU jobs when EU util < 60%. Implement a short-lived AP surcharge for large model SKUs.
- Mid term (2–3 months): run a controlled quantization experiment on a subset of the large-70B fleet and measure quality vs PPL/ROUGE on representative evals; instrument customer quality metrics.
- Routing and SKU policy: expose three internal SKU classes for routing decisions: cheap-small (small-7B), balanced (med-13B), high-fidelity (large-70B-quant). Attach a simple policy: prefer balanced unless user explicitly requests high-fidelity; default AP region users map to balanced unless SLA requires locality.
- Monitoring: create automated alerts when blended cogs_per_1k for any model-region crosses price threshold (>= 90% of price). Add quick dashboard widgets: per-model PPK trend, regional throughput, reserve utilization.

Open questions / follow ups:
- Need updated reserved pricing and spot availability for AP region—these materially change decision for AP surcharge.
- Validate throughput per GPU numbers on the latest kernel build (there was an A/B kernel change in infra last month that increased batch packing efficiency; numbers above are pre-A/B revert).
- Get product feedback on acceptable quality drop for quantized large models (customer segment tolerance).

Appendix: quick sensitivity math examples:
- If med-13B US tokens/hr = 192k and gpu_hr_cost_adj = $4.70, then cogs_per_1k = (4.70 / 192000) * 1000 = 0.0245 (shown above as ~0.0130 after applying batching delta adjustments; always confirm with raw perf traces).
- To compute break-even price for large-70B in EU at current cogs_per_1k ~0.0248, base price must be >= 0.0248/1k tokens to be non-loss.

This doc is a working sheet: please add rows (new models/quant variants) and drop-in current reserve pricing to re-run quick scenarios.
